variants.title: Find the throughput ceiling
variants.context: A bottleneck is the stage that limits completed work. Here every request visits each stage once and all stage capacities use the same unit.
variants.prompt: Network capacity is 1000, service capacity 800, and database capacity 200 requests/second. Ignoring other costs, what is the highest sustainable throughput?
variants.explanation: The slowest stage allows 200 requests/second. Capacities do not add along a sequential path.

mistakes.feedback: That adds the three capacities. Capacities do not add along a sequential path.
That is the fastest stage. The slowest stage sets the ceiling.

variants.title: Estimate an optimization
variants.context: End-to-end time is the sum of sequential stages. Improving one stage only removes time from that stage.
variants.prompt: A request takes 200 ms. One stage contributes 100 ms. You halve that stage’s time; all other stages stay unchanged. What is the new total?
variants.hint: Subtract the original stage time, then add its new time.

mistakes.feedback: That halves the whole request. Only the one stage improves.
That adds the halved stage instead of replacing its original time.

variants.title: Test a bottleneck hypothesis
variants.context: Bottleneck analysis connects a user symptom to evidence and a controlled change.
variants.prompt: Checkout is slow. Order the investigation.

items.text: Trace where the request spends time.
Change the suspected limiting stage in a controlled test.
Compare end-to-end latency under the same load.

variants.hint: Observe, explain, change one cause, then verify the whole outcome.
variants.explanation: A component improvement matters when the user-visible outcome improves.

variants.title: Test a bottleneck hypothesis
variants.context: Bottleneck analysis connects a user symptom to evidence and a controlled change.
variants.prompt: A queue keeps growing. Order the investigation.

items.text: Find the stage whose capacity is exhausted.
Increase that stage’s capacity in a controlled test.
Check queue growth and completion rate again.

variants.hint: Observe, explain, change one cause, then verify the whole outcome.
variants.explanation: Compare the system before and after under comparable arrivals.

variants.title: Test a bottleneck hypothesis
variants.context: Bottleneck analysis connects a user symptom to evidence and a controlled change.
variants.prompt: A database connection pool appears saturated. Order the investigation.

items.text: Check how long connections are held and why.
Test a targeted fix with the same workload.
Check both request latency and database pressure.
Measure request wait time for a connection.

variants.hint: Observe, explain, change one cause, then verify the whole outcome.
variants.explanation: A larger pool alone can move pressure into the database.
